programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry sees dollar signs when he learns that young Hayden’s father is sick, very rich, and planning to leave something to Hayden’s favourite staff members. Already established as Hayden’s Number One teacher, Gerry awaits his monetary gift with eager anticipation, only to discover that his ‘gift’ is legal guardianship of Hayden. But Gerry’s initial disappointment is quickly remedied by the financial contribution that accompanies said guardianship. Unfortunately, raising a child turns out to be a tad more expensive than Gerry had anticipated. Meanwhile, Robert becomes co-principal and takes every opportunity to ensure that all staff and students understand that he is no longer Lisa’s subordinate. Nisha jumps in on some innocent student games during recess, only to injure herself and ruin everything.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s almost March break and all of the staff members seem to have saved enough money for a vacation, except for Gerry. Gerry manages to establish a surprisingly positive rapport with the inmates, only to find himself the accidental drug mule for one of his new students. Meanwhile, Simon has been teaching an ESL class and becomes convinced one of his students has a much better grasp of the English language than he’s been letting on. Nisha has been tutoring students at their homes, but finds the work environments difficult to navigate.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After one of Gerry’s students skips a detention for a theatre rehearsal, Gerry confronts the student mid-rehearsal and unleashes a barrage of vitriol that impresses director Emma so much so that she immediately fires the student, offering Gerry the starring role instead. Will this be the birth of a brilliant thespian? In an effort to motivate her lazy students, Bobbi equips them all with heart monitors. At first, her efforts appear to be successful, but Bobbi soon finds herself unintentionally tracking a different type of student exercise. Nisha’s been having trouble getting her class to respect her authority, but has figured out that she can manipulate them into paying attention by crying in the classroom. Robert cracks down on Nisha’s unconventional tactic, only to find himself taking a page out of her book.

programme.desc: Gerry is turning forty, and after finding a letter he wrote to himself ten years earlier, he becomes acutely aware of everything he has failed to accomplish. programme.title: Mr. D

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry volunteers to cover Simon’s girls’ volleyball team, assuring Bobbi that he won’t ruin their playoff run. But when Bill reminds him of their friend’s wedding on Saturday, Gerry’s afraid he’ll miss his shot with Suzie the bridesmaid. He sets out to do the only right thing: throw the first game, thereby freeing up his Saturday. Meanwhile, staff and students are finding they don’t have enough time between classes to get all the way across the school, so Robert devises a plan to get everybody moving through the hallways more quickly. When Trudy learns she has an allergy to soy nuts, Lisa insists she provide a photo for Xavier’s Allergy Wall, in the event of an emergency.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Lisa starts a friendly ‘Teacher of the Month’ competition and it’s no surprise when Mr. Dwyer wins the first one. Gerry feels slighted and is determined to find a way to earn next month’s title. When word gets out that a lurker has been spotted in the neighbourhood, Gerry sets out to catch him. Of course, catching a lurker is no small feat and Gerry must use some rather unconventional tactics if he’s to succeed. Meanwhile, Robert has been working on an art installation made up of photos of Xavier’s staff and students. Bobbi is upset to find she has seemingly been excluded from the project and confronts him about his unresolved feelings for her. At the same time, an unexpected feud develops between Dwyer and Nisha when they discover that they’ve been using the same catchphrase. After all, “Every day’s a holiday” can only belong to one.

Gerry tasks Simon with keep hot sub Shane away from hot sub Mary, until Gerry can lock that down. programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry walks in on Trudy and Emma watching a viral video of a bus driver being bullied by students. After learning about a crowdfunding effort that raised money for the poor bus driver, he recruits Simon to help him stage a ‘bullying’ incident on the bus, in which he is to be the sad victim. Meanwhile, Bobbi takes a dozen pregnancy tests and finally accepts that she’s pregnant. When the tests are discovered, she finds herself roped into Robert’s misguided hunt for twelve frightened pregnant young students.. Dwyer has a new lady in his life and seems happier than he’s been in a long time. Nisha couldn’t be more pleased for him, until she discovers that his new love interest bears a striking resemblance to the sketch composite of the suspect in his late wife’s murder case.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s almost the end of the school year, and Gerry seems to be the only teacher at Xavier who hasn’t been offered a full-time contract for next fall. Even after Gerry plays the marriage card, it seems Lisa can’t guarantee him anything beyond fulltime substitute. Unwilling to accept this fate, Gerry gets an idea to start his own Charter school. Meanwhile, Robert and Bobbi interview applicants to fill Bobbi’s position while she’s away on maternity leave. Her initial concern about finding a qualified candidate is replaced with a deep insecurity that she won’t even be missed when the candidates prove quite overqualified. Lisa pulls out all the stops to throw an end-of-year faculty party. But when her efforts seem to go unappreciated, Lisa makes a bold move.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: It’s a new school year and Gerry has finally achieved his goal: full-time Phys Ed! But when he finds out how Bobbi’s been teaching Phys Ed, Gerry’s appalled, and sets out to teach the course the way it should be taught…or the way he thinks it should be taught, anyways. Meanwhile, Dwyer learns the ropes to his newly appointed position of Vice Principal; and Nisha, fresh off her camp counsellor summer job, struggles to reset boundaries with three seniors.
programme.sub-title: Gerry Wants to Make Phys Ed Great Again

programme.title: Crafting Cabinet Doors: Materials & Cutting Techniques
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: Crafting Cabinet Doors: Materials & Cutting Techniques
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: Meherio
programme.desc: Documentary following the Tahitian professional windsurfer Mathilde Zampieri.

programme.title: A Gallery Without Walls
programme.desc: In a secluded spot at the eastern end of New Zealand's Waiheke Island lies Connells Bay where John and Jo Gow, passionate and well-known in art and sculpture circles have established the Connells Bay Sculpture Park where art and nature are united to create special spaces for site specific sculpture.

programme.title: Jaffa: A Guide to Gentrification
programme.desc: Jaffa, once a major port in the Middle East and the sister city of Tel Aviv, “the most expensive city in the world” per The Economist, has grown into an international tourist center, a coveted destination and last but not least a true real estate gem.

programme.title: On The Inside Of a Military Dictatorship
programme.desc:
“On the Inside of a Military Dictatorship” takes its audience back to when the military made their master plan for a so-called disciplined democracy in Myanmar and wrote a very scripted role for their enemy no. 1; Aung San Suu Kyi. In a dramatic way, the film builds the character- and story set-up to take us anew into the crisis we know from the news – however, with a radically different perspective. The story is based on unique acces to the key players in this complicated reality, including Aung San Suu Kyi and previous President Thein Sein.
It’s the story of how power struggles unfold and how political enemies can end up being closer than the ones they claim to fight for: the people. The audience gets deeper and deeper into this complex world of power driven by peculiar characters and even astrology.

programme.title: The Loop
programme.desc: A small discovery leads two adventurers to climb the cliffs of their home island and make unexpected discoveries. Their challenge, obstructed by tons of pollution that is swept up the coast every day, marks a shift in perspective and their interaction with our environment.

programme.title: Desert Coffee
programme.desc: Slab City is a squatter community in the Sonoran Desert and 'the last free place in America'. The inhabitants live off-the-grid in broken trailers or old school buses with no running water, electricity or sewage system. Their closest neighbours are the Marine Corps, who practice aerial bombing in the area.

programme.title: The Negotiators How To Make Peace
programme.desc: Featuring an inquisitive look at the identity and evolution of those people who seek solutions to armed conflicts in the 21st century.Negotiators talk about their work, their evaluation of the situations, and also the personal cost to them.

programme.title: The Indian Queen
programme.desc: Septuagenarians Alan and Pat Braithwaite set out on the adventure of a lifetime, driving 5,600 km across India and back in a tiny Morgan three-wheeler sports car.

programme.title: The River Between Us
programme.desc: A River Between Us tells the story of the oldest and most bitterly disputed water war in the West today. The film's primary focus is the struggle for justice on the Klamath River, where forty years of bad blood between the local farmers, ranchers, Native Tribes, members of the Tea Party, state politicians and federal government have created one of this country's worst environmental crises. Most importantly, as part of the largest restoration project in American history, A River Between Us provides the solution to ending this generations-old conflict: in order to save a river, you must first heal a people.

programme.title: Elliott Erwitt, Silence Sounds Good
programme.desc:
Directed by Erwitt's previous assistant, a documentary about the Magnum photographer, tirelessly dedicated to his art, and, in his own words, "very serious about not being serious".
Director

programme.title: Meltdown in Dixie
programme.desc: In the wake of the 2015 Charleston Massacre, a battle erupts in Orangeburg, South Carolina between the Sons of Confederate Veterans and an ice cream shop owner forced to fly the Confederate flag in his parking lot. MELTDOWN IN DIXIE explores the broader role of Confederate symbolism in 21st century America and the lingering racial oppression which these symbols help maintain.

programme.title: Idomeni
programme.desc: Idomeni is both a place suspended in time, and a film shaped by scenes from the parallel lives of adults and children in the camp. The children do not go to school but live in their own world and take care of each other, having little contact with their surroundings. The film catches their bubble and shows: they are tomorrow's Europe. It is a place where you are suspended in time. You cannot move forward and you cannot go back. You are confined. But it is not a prison, it is a refugee camp. Refugee camps are usually located far away from the rest of society and they become like worlds of their own. This is a film about life in the camps. The film does not explore the dramatic events of the journey but the seemingly still and slowed down moments in the camps.

programme.title: Birds Without Wings
programme.desc: Two adults who grew up in the slums of Delhi strive to give new wings to the kids bounded by the shackles of poverty, drugs, and society.

programme.title: War Peace
programme.desc: War/Peace documentary film is re-introducing the radical student activists from the late 60s. Ex-leaders of The Weather Underground movement Bill Ayers and Bernardine Dohrn. For decades the government and press have tried their best to silence them. This film will serve as an historical reminder of what happened the last time a group of young minds planned to take over an unpopular government in Washington.

programme.title: PostCard From Afghanistan
programme.desc: Comedian Mike King faces a stand-up gig like none other when asked to perform for American troops based in Afghanistan. King also meets with Kiwi soldiers situated in Kabul, Bagram, and Bamyan and talks about how they are helping rebuild and provide security in the war-torn country. During his journey, he learns about life in Afghanistan for these soldiers and the roles they play in the decades-long war. programme.title: Music For Elephants

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: Blame Game
programme.desc: Blame Game explores the challenges but also the possible solutions - some very simple - that could reduce waste, take advantage of an impressive skill-set, alleviate poverty and help our environment.

programme.title: Escape From Room 18
programme.desc: John Daly, an ex-Neo Nazi, fled to Israel when his gang tried to kill him for being Jewish. An old Skinhead friend finds John 25 years later and suggests they visit concentration camps in an effort to make amends for their past.

programme.title: Golden Age
programme.desc: Extravaganza and glamour lining up in an existential contest against isolation, slackening limbs and lethargy. With unique access behind the scences, the Palace in Miami is shown as a buzzing and luzurious senior living community, repeatedly voted "American's Number One". The seniors live in a world full of parties and entertainment, but the Palace is also a thrivin business.... Who said that old age has to be boring? Golden Age opens the doors to the Palace, a retirement home of the kind that you have never seen before, in Miami. Gildings, ostentatious chandeliers, marble floors; like a cross between a luxury hotel and an Americanised copy of Versailles, the place is presented by its developers as the most beautiful retirement home in the US. The residents here are pampered by an army of employees devoted to their every whim, in a oermanent party atmosphere. This abundance of luxury, extravagance and entertainment is nonetheless not enough to remove the anxieties of those who live there. Nor can it hide the intention of the investors for whome old age is above all source of income and a growing market. Golden Age takes us on a journey into this baroque universe which tries to suppress the fear of death through dollars, questioning, in a dizzying visual whirlwind, our relationship to old age in its most universal aspect.

programme.title: The Good Death
programme.desc:
Janette is terminally ill and wants to die in a dignified way. Muscular dystrophy, the illness that Janette suffers from, has affected her family for generations. Janette's mother was wheelchair bound for decades, a prisoner in her own body. Janette refuses to wait for death in unbearable pain and opts for physician-assisted suicide. Before leaving on her last journey she has to explain her intention to her family members and close friends. Her son Simon has also inherited this illness and, therefore, has much more sympathy for her decision than his sister Bridget. If no cure for this illness is found, he will face the same decision process as his mother. Both children try to convince Janette to postpone her death. Do we own our life or does it own us?
The film uses feature film techniques, and engaging characters and their stories interwoven with Janette’s testament.

programme.title: Haunted Lake Lanier
programme.desc: Dive into the murky secrets of Lake Lanier, where restless spirits haunt its waters. Uncover forgotten graves, encounter the mysterious Lady of the Lake, and witness ghostly apparitions. This exploration delves into the eerie history of Lake Lanier.

programme.title: 300 Trillion The Debt Trap
programme.desc: The film explores the significance of our debt situation, looking at true stories behind the situation, from a debtors' prison in Mississippi to the world's most notoriously indebted country.

programme.title: 100 Million Views
programme.desc: We set out a mission to discover the secrets of what makes a video go viral. Along the way we meet with Youtube stars past and present, from the viral sensations of yesterday to the modern breed of Influencers who have fine-tuned the art of audience building, algorithmic tampering and fan engagement. But as our journey takes us deeper into the heart of the Youtube machine, questions emerge about how exactly this platform that was supposed to democratise entertainment, has evolved. With dark humour and caustic wit, 100 Million Views uncovers the truth about a platform that promised transparency and democracy, but hides an exploitative, censored and unaccountable underbelly.

programme.desc: Melody, Stella and Lucia are three women from three different countries; they all have their own view of life and have already given birth

programme.title: Meherio
programme.desc: Documentary following the Tahitian professional windsurfer Mathilde Zampieri.

programme.title: A Gallery Without Walls
programme.desc: In a secluded spot at the eastern end of New Zealand's Waiheke Island lies Connells Bay where John and Jo Gow, passionate and well-known in art and sculpture circles have established the Connells Bay Sculpture Park where art and nature are united to create special spaces for site specific sculpture.

programme.title: Jaffa: A Guide to Gentrification
programme.desc: Jaffa, once a major port in the Middle East and the sister city of Tel Aviv, “the most expensive city in the world” per The Economist, has grown into an international tourist center, a coveted destination and last but not least a true real estate gem.

programme.title: On The Inside Of a Military Dictatorship
programme.desc:
“On the Inside of a Military Dictatorship” takes its audience back to when the military made their master plan for a so-called disciplined democracy in Myanmar and wrote a very scripted role for their enemy no. 1; Aung San Suu Kyi. In a dramatic way, the film builds the character- and story set-up to take us anew into the crisis we know from the news – however, with a radically different perspective. The story is based on unique acces to the key players in this complicated reality, including Aung San Suu Kyi and previous President Thein Sein.
It’s the story of how power struggles unfold and how political enemies can end up being closer than the ones they claim to fight for: the people. The audience gets deeper and deeper into this complex world of power driven by peculiar characters and even astrology.

programme.title: The River Between Us
programme.desc: A River Between Us tells the story of the oldest and most bitterly disputed water war in the West today. The film's primary focus is the struggle for justice on the Klamath River, where forty years of bad blood between the local farmers, ranchers, Native Tribes, members of the Tea Party, state politicians and federal government have created one of this country's worst environmental crises. Most importantly, as part of the largest restoration project in American history, A River Between Us provides the solution to ending this generations-old conflict: in order to save a river, you must first heal a people.

programme.title: Elliott Erwitt, Silence Sounds Good
programme.desc:
Directed by Erwitt's previous assistant, a documentary about the Magnum photographer, tirelessly dedicated to his art, and, in his own words, "very serious about not being serious".
Director

programme.title: Meltdown in Dixie
programme.desc: In the wake of the 2015 Charleston Massacre, a battle erupts in Orangeburg, South Carolina between the Sons of Confederate Veterans and an ice cream shop owner forced to fly the Confederate flag in his parking lot. MELTDOWN IN DIXIE explores the broader role of Confederate symbolism in 21st century America and the lingering racial oppression which these symbols help maintain.

programme.title: Idomeni
programme.desc: Idomeni is both a place suspended in time, and a film shaped by scenes from the parallel lives of adults and children in the camp. The children do not go to school but live in their own world and take care of each other, having little contact with their surroundings. The film catches their bubble and shows: they are tomorrow's Europe. It is a place where you are suspended in time. You cannot move forward and you cannot go back. You are confined. But it is not a prison, it is a refugee camp. Refugee camps are usually located far away from the rest of society and they become like worlds of their own. This is a film about life in the camps. The film does not explore the dramatic events of the journey but the seemingly still and slowed down moments in the camps.

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: The River Between Us
programme.desc: A River Between Us tells the story of the oldest and most bitterly disputed water war in the West today. The film's primary focus is the struggle for justice on the Klamath River, where forty years of bad blood between the local farmers, ranchers, Native Tribes, members of the Tea Party, state politicians and federal government have created one of this country's worst environmental crises. Most importantly, as part of the largest restoration project in American history, A River Between Us provides the solution to ending this generations-old conflict: in order to save a river, you must first heal a people.

programme.title: Birds Without Wings
programme.desc: Two adults who grew up in the slums of Delhi strive to give new wings to the kids bounded by the shackles of poverty, drugs, and society.

programme.title: War Peace
programme.desc: War/Peace documentary film is re-introducing the radical student activists from the late 60s. Ex-leaders of The Weather Underground movement Bill Ayers and Bernardine Dohrn. For decades the government and press have tried their best to silence them. This film will serve as an historical reminder of what happened the last time a group of young minds planned to take over an unpopular government in Washington.

programme.title: PostCard From Afghanistan
programme.desc: Comedian Mike King faces a stand-up gig like none other when asked to perform for American troops based in Afghanistan. King also meets with Kiwi soldiers situated in Kabul, Bagram, and Bamyan and talks about how they are helping rebuild and provide security in the war-torn country. During his journey, he learns about life in Afghanistan for these soldiers and the roles they play in the decades-long war. A siren signaling an "indirect airstrike" causes King and his team to scramble for shelter as they experience first-hand terror of war.

programme.title: Music For Elephants
programme.desc: An incredible, unique and moving documentary about a concert pianist, who plays music to blind, injured and orphaned elephants with amazing results. At a sanctuary on the shores of the iconic River Kwai in Thailand, Paul Barton plays the works of world’s greatest composers to endangered Asian elephants and reveals their secret love of music.

programme.title: Grain: Analog Renaissance
programme.desc: Today, the art world and beyond is obsessed with shooting analog. Whether it’s a fashion house seeking to bring a new edge to their creative work, an amateur perusing eBay for the perfect vintage Polaroid, or an influencer attempting to capture a comforting retro aesthetic on social media, analog photography has piqued the interest of people everywhere. Is this resurgence a backlash against digital photography? Is it just a trend perpetuated by our desire for authentically in an increasingly superficial world? Or is it something else entirely? We explore the stories of those committed to using film in modern day photography

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.desc: Lady Elliot is a small coral cay on the southern part of the Great Barrier Reef. The Island is made up of coral. It looks pretty spectacular from the air with aqua blue water surrounding the entire island. It’s almost like Disneyland for the underwater world

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join John Plaskett as he discovers the vibrant history of the Italian city of Brescia. Home to several UNESCO World Heritage Sites this city has gone out of its way to preserve its colourful history. From the remains of Ancient Roman houses in the Santa Guila Museum Complex to the astronomical clock located in Piazza della Loggia. With every corner you turn there is more history looking back at you.

programme.title: Escape To Paradise
programme.desc: The Caribbean has always been a dream destination for holidaymakers dreaming of that perfect getaway, and Antigua has long been a favourite for the British. Of course, it spent several centuries under British rule, and the connections endure in names such as Nelson’s Dockyard and English Harbour. Today though, it’s the 365 beaches, year round sunshine, and colourful cocktails that bring the visitors.

Today though, it’s the 365 beaches, year round sunshine, and colourful cocktails that bring the visitors.

programme.title: Essence Of India
programme.desc:
Samira is in New York, getting ready for an exciting trip back home to India, where she re-visits Indian cuisine with her New York culinary trained eye. She packs her bags and sets off.
New York’s signature street food is the hot dog. In India, street food is a highly developed cuisine all on its own, going back hundreds of years. Samira has her own take on the shammi kabab and turns them into mini burgers in her kitchen, before traipsing all over New Delhi in her Essence of India auto rickshaw devouring the hearty Samosa, the succulent Kathi wraps, the moorishly moist Biryanis and even ends up taking over a street cart with a smorgasbord of sweet, tangy and spicy Indian chaat.

programme.title: Essence Of India
programme.desc:
The whole world loves a good curry, and living in New York, Samira loves to make curries, Indian, South East Asian and the Western stew, but she heads back to India where she learns how to make some of India’s finest curries.
Here is the story of ultimate deliciousness -- the tale of the curry. The desire to perfect her skills, sets her off on a curry trail, seeking out the best chefs in Delhi and getting them to spill their secrets.
This episode travels through the kitchens of master chefs, who created the king of all curries, The Butter Chicken, reintroduces the authentic korma, a recipe that has been tweaked across the globe and tells the story of the Raja Mirch, the hottest pepper in the world.

programme.desc:
Samira is all excited for the Tandoori Party.
The world loves to BBQ and India has some of the oldest forms – Tandoori cooking. Samira takes a fresh approach to Tandoori cuisine and the grill that goes back thousands of years.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join John Plaskett as he discovers the vibrant history of the Italian city of Brescia. Home to several UNESCO World Heritage Sites this city has gone out of its way to preserve its colourful history. From the remains of Ancient Roman houses in the Santa Guila Museum Complex to the astronomical clock located in Piazza della Loggia. With every corner you turn there is more history looking back at you.

programme.title: Escape To Paradise
programme.desc: The Caribbean has always been a dream destination for holidaymakers dreaming of that perfect getaway, and Antigua has long been a favourite for the British. Of course, it spent several centuries under British rule, and the connections endure in names such as Nelson’s Dockyard and English Harbour. Today though, it’s the 365 beaches, year round sunshine, and colourful cocktails that bring the visitors.

programme.title: Bill Code
programme.desc: News - In this episode of Hope & Health, Mathew Embry speaks with retired anesthesiologist Bill Code about living with multiple sclerosis for nearly three decades. Diagnosed in 1996, Bill shares how his medical background and personal experience shaped his long-term approach to managing MS. The conversation explores hyperbaric oxygen therapy, omega-3 supplementation, the microvascular theory of MS, and the role of blood flow and cellular energy in neurological health. Bill also reflects on discipline, daily habits, and why many of the strategies he uses extend beyond MS to broader brain and recovery science.

programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Along the way she faced several major challenges including a serious car accident, a hysterectomy, and the effects of menopause, all while continuing to pursue optimal health and eventually stepping onto the competitive bodybuilding stage in her 50s. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.

programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Along the way she faced several major challenges including a serious car accident, a hysterectomy, and the effects of menopause, all while continuing to pursue optimal health and eventually stepping onto the competitive bodybuilding stage in her 50s. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.

programme.title: Angie Gensler
programme.desc: News - Angie Gensler is a mother and personal trainer who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2004. In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Angie about her diagnosis and why she ultimately chose not to pursue drug treatments. Instead, she focused on lifestyle changes including diet, exercise, and daily discipline. Along the way she faced several major challenges including a serious car accident, a hysterectomy, and the effects of menopause, all while continuing to pursue optimal health and eventually stepping onto the competitive bodybuilding stage in her 50s. Her story is an inspiration to anyone navigating a difficult diagnosis.

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E09 - Private Military Contractors
programme.desc: The practice of hiring private armies goes back to ancient times, and the mystique associated with the mercenary warrior has been the subject of many historical studies and fictional characterizations. Using its “sub-second” analysis techniques and intimate first-person footage, CQB reveals the backgrounds, training and equipment of today’s “soldiers for hire” and how private armies are re-shaping the way conflicts are conducted around the world.

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation
programme.desc: Finding a mate, building a nest, and raising kids are all part of the whole reproductive behavior thing. But it’s not as easy as it sounds. First, you’ve got to sift through lots of possible partners to find the one with the best genes to keep your family line going. Nesting involves finding some space and then guarding it fiercely, while raising the little ones takes loads of energy as you have to feed, teach, and keep them safe until they grow up. This episode dives into the ins and outs of how creatures go about their reproductive business.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation

Nesting involves finding some space and then guarding it fiercely, while raising the little ones takes loads of energy as you have to feed, teach, and keep them safe until they grow up. This episode dives into the ins and outs of how creatures go about their reproductive business.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E04 - Battle Plans
programme.desc: Surviving in the wild often means being able to fight and win. This fighting strategy is called agonism and is used to set ranks, get resources, claim territory, and attract partners. There's no certainty in the wild, but animals that get good at agonism have a better shot at living to see another day.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E04 - Battle Plans

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E11 - Counter Terrorism
programme.desc: Following the September 11 attacks, military presence became commonplace in New York and other American cities, and the counter terrorism forces were effectively given a “blank cheque” when it came to ensuring that another terrorist incident would never take place on American soil. This episode of CQB takes an in–depth look at who was selected to occupy elite anti-terrorist positions, what they were trained for, and how they were equipped: when opposing forces are using commercial airliners and chemical weapons, countermeasures are by necessity complicated and varied. CQB takes an intimate look at what it was like to be an officer on alert for chemical attacks in Washington DC, or an army reservist monitoring suspicious activities on the streets of NYC.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E11 - Counter Terrorism

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E12 - French Foreign Legion
programme.desc: No country other than France operates an elite military force that invites foreign nationals to serve in its ranks. With a reputation for being a safe haven for individuals with questionable pasts, the French Foreign Legion is a true mercenary army that has garnered significant respect within the global special operations community. This episode of CQB examines a raid by the Foreign Legion on a small airport in Iraq during the 1990 Gulf War, exploring the nature of the Legion, how it differs from other special forces, and how it prepares for a wide variety of close quarter battle scenarios in conflict situations around the world.

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E43 - Diana A Day In The Life
programme.desc: When Diana got engaged, she was constantly in the media's eyes. Throughout her life, she focused on her sons and committed herself to charity work, like speaking out against land mines. Diana used her fame to bring attention to this and other important issues. This well-researched show takes a closer look at one of the 20th century's most amazing people. With never-before-seen footage, it shows her path from a shy teen to becoming the beloved Diana, Princess of Wales, including touching moments from her last days.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E13 - Who is the King?
programme.desc: It is estimated that there are approximately 8.7 million different species of animals on Earth. Each has developed unique, specific and often deadly survival techniques and skills for survival. How do we choose a favourite from such a vast array of spectacular and beautiful creatures?
programme.sub-title: Wild Ones - S01:E13 - Who is the King?

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E01 - Naturally Breathtaking
programme.desc: Do you know where in the world the last untouched glacier is? Where is the highest and the smallest waterfall? Which desert is the driest or the largest? Would you like to know where the most inaccessible mountains, the lowest point of the oceans or the great salt deserts are? This series offers all the answers.In the first episode, we discover breathtaking glaciers in Argentina, infinite plane in the middle of Europe, thermal miracles of Hungary, stalactite caves protected by UNESCO and the most active volcano in New Zealand – White island.
programme.sub-title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E01 - Naturally Breathtaking

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E02 - Naturally Dramatic
programme.desc: This episode describes the greatest miracle of nature that could be created by the human brain. The Loch Ness monster. It looks that is does not exist but thousands of visitors still come to see the lovely lake and to hear tales about it. Not only Nessi, but the Scottish high lands are the miracle of nature.Then we quickly visit Andalusia and remove our hat in front of the majestic mountains of Sierra Nevada.The deepest lake in the world is found in Siberia. We will talk about Baikal, the natural miracle of Russia.
programme.sub-title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E02 - Naturally Dramatic

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E03 - Naturally Diverse
programme.desc: The episode focuses on the Arabian peninsula. The endless red desert in Oman contrasts with Yemen ́s island of Socotra. The endemic crabs from Socotra compete with sea turtles who gather on a single beach in Oman to lay their eggs. And, it is also claimed that the petrified rock formation is of Noah's Ark.
programme.sub-title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E03 - Naturally Diverse

programme.title: Survival Science - S01:E08 - Surviving Nature's Fury

programme.sub-title: Survival Science - S01:E08 - Surviving Nature's Fury

programme.title: Desperate Hours - S01:E01 - Volcanoes
programme.desc: The Greatest Show on Earth is also the most ferocious. Desperate Hours looks at the destructive force of volcanoes and examines the eruptions in Montserrat which devastated half a Caribbean Island, the 1973 eruption on the Icelandic island of Heimaey, the 2010 eruption Eyjafjallajökull which blocked air travel in Europe, the Merapi eruption in Indonesia, and Mount Nyiragongo in Congo, and the super-volcano in Yellowstone.

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E05 - Masters of Attack
programme.desc: Carnivores can't just pick their meals off trees. To survive, they have to use every trick they've got to catch food that's just as keen on staying alive as they are. If their prey hides, they have to find it. If it runs, they must chase it. They have to track it if it's hard to pin down and beat it if it fights back. The predator might use its strength for the final blow, but the real effort lies in the strategy.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E05 - Masters of Attack

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E06 - Devious Defenses
programme.desc: Animals can employ a number of different defenses in order to withstand an attack. Some seek safety in herds, some hide in plain sight, some meet aggression with even stronger aggression, and some build fortresses. Whatever the strategy it is clear that animals will do whatever it takes to survive the wild.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E06 - Devious Defenses
